aspiring.name: Aspiring product manager
aspiring.goal: Understand the job, learn to think like a product manager, and be ready for a first interview.

steps.title: Read what a product manager does
steps.why: Start with the job itself, so every later lesson has a place to sit.
The idea behind most good product questions: what progress is the person after?
Learn to keep what you saw apart from what you assume.
Practise that skill on a made-up user.
Learn to test the riskiest idea cheaply.
Choosing what not to build is half the job.
Work out why someone bought, from behaviour.

steps.title: Learn the CIRCLES method
steps.why: A structure for design questions, in motion.
See how an idea becomes something an engineer can build.
The core move in every metric question.
Find where people leave, and whether they stay.
Your first full diagnosis, with evidence on request.
Find out where you stand across the skills.

steps.title: Work through the question bank
steps.why: Rehearse answers, by category.
A timed mock with follow-ups and a rubric.

steps.title: Check your resume
steps.why: Make the proof visible before you apply.

working.name: Working product manager
working.goal: Find your weak spots, close them with harder cases, and test yourself under time.

steps.why: Start by finding the gaps.
Sharpen how you argue for a trade-off.
Read retention honestly.
Run and read experiments without fooling yourself.
A diagnosis where the baseline hides the real fall.
A diagnosis where the cause is outside your system.
A diagnosis with a trade-off and a tempting wrong story.
Learn from the user at the edge.
Separate what people say from what they do.
Timed mocks, scored against a rubric.

steps.title: Review your competency levels
steps.why: See where you moved and what is still weak.

technical.name: Technical product manager
technical.goal: Build the technical ground to discuss systems, trade-offs and AI with engineers and in interviews.

steps.why: The vocabulary of every technical conversation.
How data choices shape the product.
Targets, caches and what must never fail.

steps.title: Read the technical skills
steps.why: The same ideas, in the interview framing.
The facts behind every AI feature decision.

steps.title: Read AI for product managers
steps.why: Evaluation, cost and when AI is the wrong tool.
A diagnosis that runs through APIs, issuers and a gateway.
A diagnosis that ends at an SDK and a release.
Practise explaining a trade-off against the clock.
